commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Bound hero checkpoint storage across cutovers (#9427)

Changes that came out of post-mortem for the [9/23
incident](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8506#issuecomment-5817400840):

1. The training-control endpoint accepts a
`request-permanent-checkpoint` header value, which saves the next step
as a permanent checkpoint in the run's output root. Hero handoffs no
longer need a forced temporary save that is then protected by hand and
copied to a durable prefix. The dashboard button still saves only
temporary checkpoints.
2. Temporary checkpoints expire after 3 days instead of 14. The live
run's newest one is at most an hour old, so the shorter TTL only removes
checkpoints left behind by replaced runs.
`temporary_checkpoint_base_path` takes the TTL as a parameter; other
callers keep 14 days.
3. The deploy-hero-change skill now hands off from a permanent
checkpoint created via the mechanism in (1), and checks object-storage
headroom first.

Part of #8506

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[storage] Add resumable verified cross-backend copies (#8900)

Add `fsutil verified-copy` for publishing large multi-object artifacts
across storage providers. GCS exposes CRC32C and sometimes MD5, while
multipart R2 ETags encode the MD5 values of individual upload parts. The
metadata therefore does not provide one checksum that can be compared
directly across the two systems. An ordinary recursive copy also has no
atomic prefix-level completion state: a preempted job can leave enough
checkpoint files for a loader to mistake a partial checkpoint for a
complete one, and a retry can mix source generations.

Bind each object to its source generation and hash source bytes while
uploading to a deterministic sibling staging prefix. R2 buckets declared
by Marin's storage router use fixed-size multipart uploads; the copy
calculates the expected ETag from the same part boundaries and compares
it with R2 metadata. Destinations without deterministic ETags are read
back and checked against the source SHA-256.

After every file from the initial source listing has a verified staging
record, promote objects with server-side within-destination copies using
the same multipart boundaries, remove staging, and write
`.verified-copy-manifest.json` last. Prefix promotion remains
object-at-a-time, so consumers must check the manifest before loading
the destination. Records under `<DST>.verified-copy-status` bind the
source identity, path, size, SHA-256, and staging identity; retries can
use them to reuse either a staged object or one already promoted before
an interruption.

For the roughly 125 GiB 67B Grug model exports tracked in #8702, staging
adds an internal R2 copy pass and transient duplicate storage. It adds
no GCS traffic beyond the original GCS-to-R2 transfer and avoids a full
client-side R2 verification read. The original transfer still incurs
retail GCS egress.

Part of #8702

commits.message:
[grafana] Project the training finish from the recent step rate (#9402)

The run status projected finish extrapolated a run's whole-life step
rate, so every outage stayed in the average and a throughput change took
days to show. It now uses the last 1,000 logged steps, sampled by step

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[drafting] Train Snowball EAGLE drafts online (#9289)

Train Snowball's EAGLE-3 draft inside the SkyRL rollout loop. Every four
policy steps, vLLM captures at most 131,072 training tokens from
verified proposal windows. A dedicated H100 DraftTrainer updates the
draft asynchronously. The promotion gate rejects a candidate if held-out
loss rises by more than 0.05 or target-token agreement falls by more
than 0.01 relative to the incumbent, then vLLM loads accepted
checkpoints at the next rollout boundary. The six-node recipe uses four
Megatron policy nodes, one DP8/EP8 rollout node, and one DraftTrainer
node. Captures and draft checkpoints live beneath the run's checkpoint
root, so the workflow does not materialize a separate hidden-state
corpus or depend on a Speculators fork.

Reusable Megatron and online-EAGLE configuration now lives in the
artifact-free `marin.rl.drafting_sft` module. It accepts concrete target
and initial-draft `StoragePath` values and returns a role plan plus
launch recipe. The Snowball experiment owns artifact adoption, dataset
dependencies, cluster placement, and graph construction. The completed
launch document is handed to the pinned `marinskyrl iris launch
--config` parser, which validates the upstream schema and derived role
allocation before Iris submission.

SkyRL runs now return `SkyRLRun` whether or not they export a policy.
`skyrl_step` skips terminal HF conversion by default, exposes the online
draft checkpoint root, and accepts `export_hf=True` when a portable
policy is needed. All five Marin call sites were audited: curriculum,
Iceball, and async-RL evaluations request the export; the TaskTrove
smoke and online-EAGLE run do not.

The clean seven-step smoke completed in 25 minutes. At step 4, the
online trainer fitted 18 sequences and held out six prompt-disjoint
sequences. The accepted candidate improved holdout target-token
agreement from 14.37% to 23.37% and reduced holdout loss from 21.10 to
17.75. Draft training took 8.39 seconds; capture, training, validation,
publication, and refresh took 31.92 seconds. All eight vLLM engines
loaded `draft-step-4` without a failed install.

The rollout counters moved from 1.2867 mean acceptance and 9.56%
proposal acceptance at step 1 to 1.3766 and 12.55% at the first fully
post-refresh step, then 1.3925 and 13.08% at step 7. These steps sampled
different prompts and generated different output lengths, so this is an
online smoke result rather than a controlled before/after speedup
estimate. The prompt-group-disjoint holdout comparison is the stronger
evidence that this update improved the draft.

The accepted 237.5 MB serving bundle is durable at
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/power/snowball-online-eagle-draft/2026.09.24.3`.
The run's capture and resumable trainer state remain under the default
14-day scratch prefix. MarinSkyRL #762 establishes that default, and the
smoke itself writes neither a full policy checkpoint nor a terminal HF
export.

The previous 12.51M-token offline fit selected its epoch-1 validation
checkpoint and changed held-out AIME mean acceptance from 1.5356 to
1.5414 in one run. [MarinSkyRL
#550](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/550) separately
qualified the managed capture, update, promotion, and refresh machinery;
its matched benchmark reported 2.0561 mean accepted tokens for the final
draft and 21.4% higher throughput than its target-only baseline.

Part of #9312

Add write-pipeline guidance for Marin experiments (#9408)

Define a write-pipeline skill and repository guidance that place
reusable concrete work in `lib/**`, artifact graph construction and
one-off wiring in `experiments/**`, and experiment-specific tests beside
the pipeline.

The guidance draws on the lazy-artifact migration (#6649), dataset
catalog conventions (#6777), and current reference, Nemotron, and
TaskTrove pipelines. It explains `apply` and direct `ArtifactStep`
binding while identifying library step builders that still cross the
placement boundary. Migrating those builders and older `StepSpec`
factories requires call-site and artifact-identity work and remains a
separate change.

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[RL] Add the async RL entry point launcher (#9256)

Add a launcher that trains the Snowball policy with MarinSkyRL's fully asynchronous RL loop on the curriculum pool and scores the terminal export on the curriculum evaluations. It renders the complete recipe, including values MarinSkyRL's base config already holds, and `--set key=value` changes one setting and gives the run its own output path.

The default preset is sized for 40 GPUs and evaluates every ten updates; smoke runs two short updates, and on_policy admits only groups the current weights sampled. The engine's data and expert parallelism go through the typed role plan.

The curriculum and iceball launchers build their SkyRL evaluation through the shared `skyrl_eval_step`, which resolves the completed policy export.

Launching this recipe needs a MarinSkyRL pin that includes marin-community/MarinSkyRL#654 and #685, which declare its fully asynchronous loop, telemetry and chat-template settings.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[eval] Add vLLM speculative-decoding evaluation (#9383)

Evalchemy and Harbor use Marin's shared `remote_inference` lifecycle. An
evaluation step accepts a plain `ModelConfig`. Experiments that produce
a target or EAGLE-3 draft declare those producer steps as dependencies
and resolve their URIs and identities in the evaluation step's config
builder. Existing external models can be adopted in place. No
metadata-only model step runs.

Each evaluation record stores the target and optional draft identities,
tokenizer URI and revision, per-run token counts, generation throughput,
and speculative-token acceptance metrics. Evalchemy reconstructs native
generation prompts before FineStore normalizes rollouts, preserving user
turns in nested request arguments. Pipeline results expose the sealed
FineStore archive paths for offline draft SFT.

PR #9289 can use this evaluation step for its control, initial-draft,
and trained-draft arms. Its experiment-specific model and draft
configuration remains there. Secret forwarding for a CoreWeave-root
launcher remains in #9312.

Part of #9312

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[inference] Honor proxy timeout in broker workers (#9361)

Brokered serves now scale the worker and request-lease deadlines with
`--proxy-timeout`, keeping both below the proxy deadline. Previously
that option changed only the proxy: a 3600-second setting still left the
worker at 180 seconds and the lease at 240 seconds, so long generations
returned 504.

The replacement GLM-5.3 serve completed a request in 383 seconds with
status 200. The incident record is [Echo
#510](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/510).

The timeout regression test passed. In a fresh macOS worktree, the full
test file had 60 passes and eight unrelated loopback-interface failures
(`No local network interface owns IPv4 address '127.0.0.1'`); the
affected safe suite passed all 212 tests in the original checkout.

Co-authored-by: Ben Feuer <benfeuer@Bens-MacBook-Pro.local>
